title: Protein preparation for LC-MS/MS analysis
author: Lihui Li
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.upjevkn
materials: Pierce high pH reverse phase column
After centrifuging at 14000 x g for 40min, the supernatant was filtered with 0.22µm filters. The filtrate was quantified with the BCA Protein Assay Kit (Bio-Rad Inc., Hercules, USA).

Following sample digestion and immediately before use, the Tandem mass tag (TMT) labeled reagents were equilibrated to room temperature, and 4-plex TMT reagent was applied to label 100μg of the peptide mixture of each sample, according to the instructions of the manufacturer (Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc., Waltham, USA).
Before LC-MS/MS analysis, the fractions were dissolved in 0.1% formic acid, according to the instructions of the manufacturer (Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc.).

steps.title: Sample Lysis and Homogenization
steps.instruction: Lyse the sample using SDT lysis buffer and homogenize the mixture.

substeps.instruction: Add SDT lysis buffer to the sample and transfer to 2ml tubes containing quartz sand with 1/4-inch ceramic beads (MP 6540-424 for tissue samples).
Homogenize the lysate twice for 60 s using an MP homogenizer (24×2, 6.0M/S).

steps.title: Protein Separation via SDS-PAGE
steps.instruction: Separate 20µg of protein per sample using SDS-PAGE.

substeps.instruction: Mix 20µg of protein per sample with 5X loading buffer.
Run the proteins on a 12.5% SDS-PAGE gel for 90 min with a constant current of 14mA.

steps.title: Filter-Aided Sample Preparation (FASP)
steps.instruction: Prepare 200μg of protein per sample for digestion using FASP.

substeps.instruction: Add 200μg of protein per sample to 30μl of SDT buffer (150mM Tris-HCl, 4% SDS, 100mM DTT, pH8.0).
Remove DTT, detergent, and low-molecular-weight components using uric acid buffer (150mM Tris-HCl, 8M urea, pH8.0).
Add 100μl iodoacetamide to block reduced cysteine residues.
Incubate the samples for 30 min in the dark.
Wash the filters three times with 100μl uric acid buffer.
Wash the filters twice with 100μl of 100mM tetraethyl-ammonium bromide (TEAB) buffer.

steps.title: Protein Digestion
steps.instruction: Digest the protein suspensions using trypsin.

substeps.instruction: Add 4μg of trypsin in 40μl of TEAB buffer to the protein suspensions.

steps.title: TMT Labeling
steps.instruction: Label protein peptides with TMT tags and treat with hydroxylamine.

substeps.instruction: Label protein peptides with TMT-126, TMT-127, TMT-128, and TMT-129 for the CG, MG, DG, and NDG groups (three biological replicates each).
Incubate for 60 min to allow the reaction to occur.
Add 8μl of 5% hydroxylamine to the sample and incubate for an additional 15 minutes.

steps.title: Sample Fractionation
steps.instruction: Fractionate TMT-labeled samples using high pH reversed-phase fractionation.

substeps.instruction: Fractionate samples into 10 fractions using a Pierce high pH reversed-phase fractionation kit via an increasing acetonitrile step-gradient elution.
